pairs.note: Force-vs-progress at similar yields, both new. AggressiveSweep cleared 30 markers in 71 steps with mean force 98 N and 75% of steps over the safe force threshold; PatientWiper cleared 29 markers across 104 steps at 29 N and 0.3% excess force. Reward separates them by less than +0.8; the maintenance perspective strongly picks B. The new reward distinguishes wipe counts handsomely but barely registers a ~70 N force gap when the yield is similar.

Positive: at similar yields (29 vs 27 wipes), the new reward *prefers* the gentler PatientWiper (force 29 N, +41.31) over a regular Maximizer (force 62 N, +38.23). Reward and maintenance now agree at this magnitude — a side-effect of the larger wipe bonus making episode length (and per-step low-pressure contact bonuses) matter more relative to small force differences.

Strong positive: a new best Maximizer cleared 65 markers at mean force 66 N (+91.74) and now decisively beats the agreed HeavyPress (44 markers at 211 N, +61.90). The maintenance, productivity, and operations perspectives all agree with reward here. Confirms the edit aligned reward and maintenance at high yields.

But the force-vs-progress disagreement at *high* force persists. A new Maximizer cleared 37 markers at 57 N (+52.28) and is still beaten by the agreed HeavyPress (44 markers at 211 N, +61.90). The maintenance perspective sharply prefers B. The wipe-bonus increase didn't change the slope of the force penalty, so a 7-marker advantage still outweighs a ~150 N force gap. The remaining option would be to raise the excess-force-penalty multiplier.
